note: The most complete ICP match in this batch and arguably the best illustration of the stated definition in the corpus. Successful is met on the business-owner test rather than by proxy: he co-founded and sold a phone company, ran a cannabis business for twelve years, bought and paid off a commercial warehouse in East County San Diego, and owns several California properties outright. Income is met on the affordability test the criterion actually applies — seven to nine thousand a month from retirement income and commercial rent, paid-off assets, and the rep's own isolation question established it was not a capacity problem: 'it sounds like we have the money. It's just more a bit of an uncertainty thing at this point' and the prospect did not dispute it. Neglected_health is the cleanest match on this criterion anywhere in the batch, and unusually it is a true match rather than a pass on the severity test: health genuinely was the neglected area while he raised a family and ran businesses, he says so directly — 'it's the years of stress eating, raising a family... it was a weakness. And then I allowed it' — and he is not in crisis. Good_to_great is explicit: 19 or 20% body fat, already training, wanting 10 to 12% and 'top 1% for 63-year-olds'. Not deconditioned is met comfortably at six foot and 186 lb with hot yoga eight times a month, daily walking, and a background in college soccer, jiu-jitsu and weightlifting. He is not remotely gym-averse. Two findings for the rollup. First, and most important: this is the second core-ICP prospect in this batch and neither closed, while the one call that did close was an edge case with no established occupation who was managing a credit card limit. If the earlier observation in icp.json is that the buying population is wider than the stated ICP, this batch adds the sharper corollary that the stated ICP is not predicting conversion at all — what separated the outcomes here was process, not fit. Second, this call is the strongest evidence yet for the standing observation that the ICP carries no clinical criterion. A prospect who scores five out of five on the stated criteria has two total hip replacements, one of them a revision, and is six weeks into a GLP-1 he intends to discontinue. There is no criterion for any of that to fail, and none of it was screened.
